status_summary: Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) directed agencies to pause disbursements under Inflation Reduction Act and infrastructure law programs for review. EPA terminated $20 billion in Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund awards to eight entities on 2025-03-11 and said on 2025-08-07 it would stop implementing the $7 billion Solar for All program; EPA's page says the July 2025 law repealed Clean Air Act section 134 and rescinded the fund's money. On 2025-09-02 a D.C. Circuit panel ruled 2-1 for EPA, but on 2026-08-04 the full court, in a one-page per curiam judgment with six of ten judges voting to affirm, reversed that decision and upheld the preliminary injunction against giving effect to the March 2025 termination notices, saying the terminations likely contravened the Inflation Reduction Act's appropriation. The judges were divided on whether the 2025 repeal changes the result for funds already obligated (five said likely not, four said EPA likely could now terminate, and one took a separate view, per the Columbia Sabin Center). On 2026-08-07 the court extended a stay at EPA's request (one report describes the freeze as agreed between EPA and the grantees) while EPA prepares a Supreme Court petition, so the funds remain frozen in practice. EPA's program page, updated 2026-09-09, does not mention the en banc ruling. On 2026-09-18 a federal district judge in Rhode Island (Judge Mary McElroy) ruled that EPA's termination of the 7 billion dollar Solar for All program was unlawful and vacated it; EPA said it was reviewing the decision and considering an appeal; no stay was reported in the source read. EPA's fiscal year 2027 budget describes some pass-through funding as not directly protecting the environment.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 directs agencies to pause disbursement of funds under Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act programs pending review (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-29).

EPA terminates $20 billion in Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund awards to eight entities (including Climate United Fund, Coalition for Green Capital and Power Forward Communities), citing conflicts of interest and oversight concerns; these are EPA's characterizations.

The 2025 reconciliation law, which EPA's page calls the Working Families Tax Cut law (understood to be Public Law 119-21, an inference), repeals Clean Air Act section 134 and rescinds the fund's remaining money, per EPA's page.
EPA announces it will stop implementing the $7 billion Solar for All program; EPA's page says the 2025 law repealed its authority and rescinded remaining funds.

The D.C. Circuit rules 2-1 for EPA, vacating a district court injunction that had blocked the terminations and holding that the grantees' claims are essentially contractual, so jurisdiction lies with the Court of Federal Claims (as described on EPA's page; the opinion itself was not fetched).

EPA's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief describes some pass-through funding as not directly protecting the environment and proposes $305 million for the clean water and drinking water state revolving funds (document filed under April 2026, exact day not confirmed, first of month used).

The D.C. Circuit, sitting en banc, issues a one-page per curiam judgment (six of ten judges voting to affirm in whole or in part) upholding the preliminary injunction against the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund terminations, which it says likely contravened the Inflation Reduction Act's appropriation, and reversing the 2025-09-02 panel decision; the judges were divided on the effect of the 2025 statutory repeal on obligated funds.

The D.C. Circuit grants EPA's request to extend a stay, keeping the National Clean Investment Fund and Clean Communities Investment Accelerator funds frozen while EPA prepares a Supreme Court appeal (per a grantee-side update); E&E News reports EPA and the grantees agreed to keep the funds frozen during the appeal.

A federal district judge in Rhode Island (Judge Mary McElroy) rules that EPA's termination of the 7 billion dollar Solar for All program was unlawful and vacates it; EPA says it is considering options for appeal.
